top_topics.topic: Plasma and Flow Control in Aerodynamics

top_cited_works.title: Effect of Three-Dimensional Plasma Actuation on the Wake of a Circular Cylinder
top_cited_works.abstract: Dielectric-barrier discharge plasma actuators were mounted on a circular cylinder in a square wave pattern for active forcing of the cylinder wake. The intermittent spacing of the buried electrodes created a spanwise-modulated blowing profile with a spanwise wavelength of four cylinder diameters, such that three-dimensional instabilities in the wake were targeted for control. Considerable spanwise variation in the wake was achieved with low-power forcing when the actuators were mounted at the location of maximum shear layer receptivity. This spanwise variation was a direct consequence of the difference in the vorticity levels of the shed vortices from the cylinder. High power forcing nearly eliminated vortex shedding, leading to a considerable amount of drag reduction as measured in the intermediate wake.

top_cited_works.title: Investigation of the cylinder wake under spanwise periodic forcing with a segmented plasma actuator
top_cited_works.abstract: The wake response to three-dimensional forcing of flow over a circular cylinder was studied. Spanwise-segmented dielectric-barrier discharge plasma actuators were mounted on the cylinder in a square wave pattern for active forcing of the cylinder wake. The buried electrodes were placed periodically to create a spanwise-modulated blowing profile, with the aim of targeting three-dimensional instabilities in the wake. Considerable spanwise variation in the wake was achieved, which was a direct consequence of the difference in the location of shed spanwise vortices from the cylinder, along with the generation of streamwise vorticity. Two distinct power levels were used for forcing the flow, with different flow response observed between the two conditions. With low power, the segmented forcing caused the large-scale spanwise structures in the forcing region to lead those in the no-forcing region, with an accompanying shift away from the centerline and generation of streamwise vorticity. While vortex shedding was not substantially attenuated with low-power forcing, the shedding in the near wake was significantly attenuated with high-power forcing. recent_works.title: Correction: The Effect of Planform Shapes on the Evolution of Bound Circulation of a Finite Wing Near an Interface
The Effect of Planform Shapes on the Evolution of Bound Circulation of a Finite Wing Near an Interface
recent_works.abstract: The evolution of circulation for a finite wing is examined near a water-to-air interface with a straight and swept wing of NACA 0015 profile with a chord length of 100 mm and an aspect ratio of 4. Main objectives for this research includes determining the impact of the planform shapes on the evolution of fluid flow around the wing and its subsequent effects on lift force. Starting submerged and at rest, the wing is brought to a constant speed before egressing through the surface of the water. A force sensor is utilized to capture force data, while a camera and laser are used to capture images for Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV). Along with planform variation, the angle of attack of the wing and speed at which it is towed is also varied. The resulting lift interface phenomena can then be compared to the fluid flow, vortex formation, and water surface deformation to find trends, while also investigating the physical nature of the interface phenomena.

recent_works.title: Stability Analysis of a Cylinder Wake With applied Harmonic Forcing
recent_works.abstract: We apply localized forcing with harmonic frequencies and study the effect on the secondary instabilities present in cylinder wakes. The main forcing frequency of interest fm is equal to 2f0, where f0 is the vortex shedding frequency. The blowing ratio Br is set to 0.8, where this parameter corresponds to the strength of the harmonic forcing. Our recent research suggests that the secondary instabilities become attenuated at Re = 1000. This conjecture arises from the isosurface plots of vorticity and observing the suppression of streamwise vorticities. Using Nektar++ we conduct direct numerical simulations (DNS) in order to recreate the secondary instabilities and subsequently apply harmonic forcing. From these results, we definitively show the suppression of the streamwise vortices and confirm the suppression of the secondary instabilities using the growth rates obtained from Floquet Stability Analysis. Applying harmonic forcing leads to spanwise uniformity in the wake, otherwise the wake is defined by spanwise kinks in shed vortices for the unforced flows.

recent_works.title: Blade-Vortex Interaction on a Twisting Flat Plate
recent_works.abstract: Vortex dynamics during parallel blade-vortex interaction (BVI) of a tandem-wing configura- tion are studied in a towing tank using planar particle image velocimetry (PIV) and force sensor data. A vortical gust is generated by applying a rapid pitching motion to a leading rigid flat plate. The generated gust collides with a trailing flat plate undergoing dynamic twisting. The interaction between the vortex and leading edge, the interaction between the vortex and the boundary layer, and the subsequent evolution of the vortex over the surface of the trailing plate are investigated for varying twisting kinematics. Vortex trajectory and strength are obtained from PIV data. The results are used to study the mechanisms of vortex decay and the effects of key parameters on vortex dynamics. The subsequent effects on the hydrodynamic forces experienced by the trailing plate are studied by analyzing force sensor data in conjunction with PIV results

recent_works.title: The Effect of Branch Angle on the Wake of a Wall-Mounted Cruciform
recent_works.abstract: We compare the flow field of a wall-mounted cruciform with three different branch angles at a Reynolds number of 15,000. A wall-mounted cruciform is a canonical representation of structures which are of interest such as piers, coral reef and oil rigs. These geometry alter the local ocean current and the sediment transport such as scouring of surrounding sediment. We show that by modifying the angle of the branching cylinder, the flow field and re-circulation zones are modified via the change in the interactions of the von Kármán shedding. The overall vorticity components generated by the cruciform is also affected by changing the branch angle. The branch angle of the cruciform redistributed the vortical structures and biased the wake profile with respect to the location of the branch. Changes in the distribution of spanwise and vertical vorticity components are provided for further insight into the vortex dynamics.
